subject: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ames <sara@acorn-analytics.com>, Acorn Procurement <procurement@acorn-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift

Hi Sara / Acorn team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited to keep this moving. Attached are the current redlines for the MSA (Acorn_MSA_v3_redline.docx) and the updated order form that reflects the 40% capacity uplift and the proposed staged ramp in Q1/Q2. High-level summary of the asks from our side: 

- Term: Redwood proposes 18-month term to align with committed capacity ramp and volume discounts.
- Capacity: 40% uplift overall; staging spelled out in OrderForm_Acorn_2028_SOW.pdf (Jan–Mar 15%, Apr–Jun 25%).
- Addendum: small exhibit to cover prefix caching and billing granularity for bursts.

Key legal points we redlined and would appreciate Acorn's feedback on:
1) Termination for convenience notice period (we proposed 60 days).
2) Indemnity carve-outs related to third-party models and open weights.
3) Audit window / evidence scope for SOC-type requests.
4) SLA credit calculation for partial-burst failures.

Could you loop in your legal (I was told Michael Lawson handles contracts) and procurement owners and let us know the absolute latest sign-off date you can commit to? Our customer success and delivery teams are targeting a Jan 2 staged kickoff if paperwork is done by Dec 15.

Next steps: if Michael can review the MSA redlines and send counterpoints by Dec 2, we can set a quick call to close. Otherwise, happy to take specific bullets to iterate more quickly.

Attachments: Acorn_MSA_v3_redline.docx, OrderForm_Acorn_2028_SOW.pdf

Cheers,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform
From: Sara Ames <sara@acorn-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acorn Procurement <procurement@acorn-analytics.com>, Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@acorn.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift

Jordan — thanks for the materials and the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before we route to legal: 

- Term: our procurement team typically prefers 12 months; can you explain the driver for 18 months (we saw the note about aligning ramp + volume discounts). Is there a bridge for customers who prefer 12 months?
- Burst billing granularity: procurement asked for a maximum daily burst cap to prevent unexpected spikes; is that in the order form?
- Audit scope: we need to confirm the types of logs/data that are in scope so we can get security sign-off quickly.

Looping in Michael (legal) and procurement. Our internal deadline to present to finance is Dec 7, so if we can get redlines back by Dec 2 that would be ideal. Also happy to do a call — are there times next week that work?

Thanks,

Sara Ames
Head of Cloud Integrations
Acorn Analytics
sara@acorn-analytics.com

From: Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@acorn.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sara Ames <sara@acorn-analytics.com>, Acorn Procurement <procurement@acorn-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift

Thanks, Jordan / Sara — I reviewed the initial redlines. A few items we'll push back on or would like alternate language for: 

- Term / automatic renewal: Acorn is open to a longer commercial commitment only if there are stronger termination rights for material outages. We will propose a 12-month initial term with an auto-extension clause that triggers only after meeting the agreed SLAs for two consecutive quarters.
- Unilateral termination: remove Redwood's clause that allows unilateral termination for convenience; propose a mutual 60-day cure period followed by termination for material breach.
- Indemnity: narrow the broadly-worded indemnity to exclude third-party model weights/OSL licensing breaches where Acorn is not supplying content.
- Audit window: request auditing notice period of 30 days and limit audit frequency to once per 12 months unless a material incident is alleged.

I'll push these points in our marked-up MSA and return redlines by EOD 2027-12-02. If Redwood can highlight the specific sections where you require the 18-month term, that will help us evaluate tradeoffs.

-Michael
Michael Lawson
Senior Counsel, Acorn Analytics
michael.lawson@acorn.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@acorn.com>, Sara Ames <sara@acorn-analytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift

Michael / Sara — thanks for the quick read. A couple of internal notes from Redwood legal on potential compromise positions so we can keep commercial momentum: 

- Term compromise: Redwood can accept a 12-month base term with a documented option for a one-time 6-month extension (to reach your stated desire for flexibility) that triggers only upon meeting volume thresholds in Exhibit D. This preserves the commercial pricing while addressing your renewal concerns.
- Termination & cure: we can change our convenience termination language to require a 60-day notice and a 30-day cure window for material issues — we would prefer to keep a limited right to wind down for security/regulatory reasons with prior notice.
- Audit: agree to 30-day notice; propose limiting scope to systems and logs relevant to the contract (we will include a sample evidence list in MSA_change_log.txt).
- Indemnity: propose narrower language that keeps standard vendor indemnities but excludes claims arising solely from model third-party licensing; we'll include proposed wording in the markup.

Ben — can you confirm the price schedule if we move to the 12+6 term option (same total committed tokens over 18 months but with billing staged as per the order form)? I want to be explicit in the redline that discounts are tied to the committed volume over the 18-month aggregate.

If Acorn is available, I suggest a 30-minute working session at 11:00 AM PT on Dec 3 to walk through the markups and the pricing tradeoffs. I'll attach the MSA_change_log.txt which lists the clauses we plan to update.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ames <sara@acorn-analytics.com>, Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@acorn.com>, Acorn Procurement <procurement@acorn-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-03T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork: MSA tweaks + staggered capacity uplift

Perfect — thanks everyone for the fast back-and-forth. Quick recap and next steps: 

- Redwood will prepare a clean redline that implements the 12 + 6 term option (pricing to reflect 18-month committed volume). Lauren will include the alternate indemnity wording and the 30-day audit notice language.
- Ben will confirm the billing schedule and confirm that discounts are applied to the 18-month aggregate (Ben, can you drop a short note by EOD?).
- Michael / Acorn: we'll review your EOD redline when you send it; thanks for prioritizing.
- Call: 11:00 AM PT on Dec 3 — proposed dial-in (I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda). Please prepare: top 3 contract items you need resolved on the call (term, indemnity scope, audit frequency).

To keep momentum, I'm also sharing a DocuSign placeholder for the order form so procurement can see the final signature flow once we land the language: https://docusign.com/placeholder/ACN-4592-orderform (placeholder link).

Attachments: OrderForm_Acorn_2028_SOW.pdf

Appreciate the partnership — we should be able to finalize by Dec 9 if the call resolves the open bullets.

Best,

Jordan Blake
